I accept that I'm stepping into the line of fire to say this, but I will defend the data corrections being applied to the satellite numbers. Scientists from separate institutions around the world confirmed that the intensity correction being applied to the satellite data was necessary due to the decaying orbit of the satellite in question. The aperture of the device points at a particular region of the planet and measures radiance per unit surface area of the emitting object (in this case, the planet itself). The device is directly measuring the intensity of a specific wavelength of radiation (chiefly infrared) and then dividing by the calculated surface area of the sample. If the satellite were closer than assumed in the surface calculation, the intensity would be lower (due to the surveyed area being smaller than estimated), resulting in a "colder" measurement. Likewise, if the orbit were decaying away from the planet, radiance measurements would be taking in radiation from a larger cross-section of the surface, resulting in a "warmer" measurement.
